arxiv-2206-09916.title: The fastest linearly converging discrete-time average consensus using buffered information
arxiv-2206-09916.creator: Amir-Salar Esteki, Hossein Moradian, Solmaz S. Kia, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2206-09916.description: Abstract In this letter, we study the problem of accelerating reaching average consensus over connected graphs in a discrete-time communication setting. Literature has shown that consensus algorithms can be accelerated by increasing the graph connectivity or optimizing the weights agents place on the information received from their neighbors.

arxiv-2303-13843.title: CompoNeRF: Text-guided Multi-object Compositional NeRF with Editable 3D Scene Layout
arxiv-2303-13843.creator: Haotian Bai HKUST(GZ), Yuanhuiyi Lyu HKUST(GZ), Lutao Jiang HKUST(GZ), Sijia Li OPPO, Haonan Lu OPPO, Xiaodong Lin OPPO, Lin Wang HKUST(GZ) HKUST
arxiv-2303-13843.description: Abstract Text-to-3D form plays a crucial role in creating editable 3D scenes for AR/VR. Recent advances have shown promise in merging neural radiance fields (NeRFs) with pre-trained diffusion models for text-to-3D object generation. However, one enduring challenge is their inadequate capability to accurately parse and regenerate consistent multi-object environments.

arxiv-2402-07556.title: Digital Twins Below the Surface: Enhancing Underwater Teleoperation Thanks: *This work was supported by EPSRC grant code EP/X024806/1, Fugro Ltd, and by the Robotics & Autonomous Systems CDT.
arxiv-2402-07556.creator: Favour O. Adetunji, Niamh Ellis, Maria Koskinopoulou, Ignacio Carlucho, Yvan R. Petillot
arxiv-2402-07556.description: Abstract Subsea exploration, inspection, and intervention operations heavily rely on remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). However, the inherent complexity of the underwater environment presents significant challenges to the operators of these vehicles. This paper delves into the challenges associated with navigation and maneuvering tasks in the teleoperation of ROVs, such as reduced situational awareness and heightened teleoperator workload.

arxiv-2409-20130.title: Reevaluation of Inductive Link Prediction
arxiv-2409-20130.creator: Simon Ott, Christian Meilicke, Heiner Stuckenschmidt
arxiv-2409-20130.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Simon Ott, Christian Meilicke, Heiner Stuckenschmidt. Within this paper, we show that the evaluation protocol currently used for inductive link prediction is heavily flawed as it relies on ranking the true entity in a small set of randomly sampled negative entities. Due to the limited size of the set of negatives, a simple rule-based baseline can achieve state-of-the-art results, which simply ranks entities higher based on the validity of their type.

arxiv-2411-12547.title: S 3 TU-Net: Structured Convolution and Superpixel Transformer for Lung Nodule Segmentation Thanks:
arxiv-2411-12547.creator: Yuke Wu 1 , Xiang Liu 1* , Yunyu Shi 1 , Xinyi Chen 1 , Zhenglei Wang 2 , YuQing Xu 3 , Shuo Hong Wang 4
arxiv-2411-12547.description: Abstract The irregular and challenging characteristics of lung adenocarcinoma nodules in computed tomography (CT) images complicate staging diagnosis, making accurate segmentation critical for clinicians to extract detailed lesion information. In this study, we propose a segmentation model, S 3 TU-Net, which integrates multi-dimensional spatial connectors and a superpixel-based visual transformer.

arxiv-2510-27208.description: Abstract Villages areas hold significant importance in the study of human-land relationships. However, with the advancement of urbanization, the gradual disappearance of spatial characteristics and the homogenization of landscapes have emerged as prominent issues. Existing studies primarily adopt a single-disciplinary perspective to analyze villages spatial morphology and its influencing factors, relying heavily on qualitative analysis methods.

pmc-11435415.title: Structural Optimization of Isoquinoline Derivatives from Lycobetaine and Their Inhibitory Activity against Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer Cells
pmc-11435415.creator: Zhuo Zhang, Qianqian Shen, Yiyi Ji, Yanjie Ma, Haiyang Hou, Huajie Yang, Yinjie Zhu, Yi Chen, Youhong Hu, David Barker, Francisco Leon
pmc-11435415.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) is a highly aggressive cancer that is resistant to hormone therapy and characterized by poor prognosis, as well as limited therapeutic options. Since the natural product lycobetaine was reported to exhibit good antitumor activities against various types of cancers, we initially simplified the scaffold of lycobetaine to obtain the active compound 1, an isoquinoline derivative with an aryl moiety substitution at the 4-position, which showed apparent antiproliferative activities against NPEC cell line LASCPC-01 in vitro.

pmc-13626716.title: Influence of limit-feeding duration on growth performance and carcass traits of finishing steers
pmc-13626716.creator: Justin J Delver, Federico Podversich, Ana C B Menezes, Warren C Rusche, Dale A Blasi, Logan R Thompson, K C Olson, John P Ritten, Zachary K F Smith
pmc-13626716.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Beef cattle are commonly limit-fed during the backgrounding period to improve feed efficiency and control fat deposition, but the effects of limit feeding duration in the finishing period remains unclear. The objective of this study was to determine the effect of limit feeding yearling beef steers for 56 or 86 d before offering ad libitum feed for the remainder of the 141-d finishing period on growth performance and carcass traits.
